claims.quote: There will be no war in the future," said M. […] ; *'  for it has become impossible, now that it is clear that war means suicide.
claims.description: Great-power war has become impossible because the new weapons make it self-destructive.

claims.quote: Certainly, everybody will be entrenched in the next war. It will be a great war of entrenchments.
claims.description: The next major war will be fought from entrenchments, with every soldier digging in under rifle and artillery fire.

claims.quote: Battles will last for days, and at the end it is very doubtful whether any decisive victory can be gained.
claims.description: Battles will last days and end in stalemate with no decisive victory.

claims.quote: But the power of rifle-fire is so great that it will be absolutely impossible for the combatants to get to close quarters with each other.
claims.description: Magazine-rifle fire will prevent opposing infantry from closing; flank and frontal assaults become impossible.

claims.quote: the war of the future, if ever it takes place, will not be fighting ; it will be terminated by famine.
claims.description: A future great war will be decided by famine and economic exhaustion rather than by battle.

claims.quote: The first thing to be borne in mind is that the next war will be a long war.
claims.description: The next great European war will be long, lasting at least two years.

claims.quote: In a war between the Triple and the Dual Alliance there would be ten millions of men under arms.
claims.description: A general war between the European alliances would mobilise about ten million men.

claims.quote: There will be practically no care for the wounded," said M. […], "for it will be impossible to find adequate shelter for the Red Cross hospital tent or for the hospital orderlies.
claims.description: Wounded will be abandoned on the battlefield because medical aid cannot operate within the fire zone.
claims.stated_time: in the war of the future

claims.quote: What is much more likely to be done is that the dying and the dead will be utilised as ramparts to strengthen the shelter trenches.
claims.description: Dead and dying soldiers will be piled up as ramparts in future battles.

claims.quote: Without competent officers, accustomed to command, it degenerates into a mere mob, and of all things in the world nothing is so helpless as a mob.
claims.description: Mass officer casualties will turn the huge conscript armies into leaderless, cowardly mobs that break down.

claims.quote: Now the whole line of communications will be exposed to dropping shots from marksmen who, from the security of thicket or hedge, will deal out sudden death without any tell-tale smoke
claims.description: Smokeless powder will let hidden marksmen harass invaders' supply lines, bleeding invading armies.

claims.quote: Neither war is any war possible, as I proceed to show, that will not entail, even upon the victorious Power, the destruction of its resources and the break-up of society.
claims.description: Any major war will destroy even the victor's resources and break up society.

claims.quote: It is estimated that such a bomb would effectively destroy all life within a range of 200 metres of the point of explosion.
claims.description: Shells charged with high explosive will break into about 1200 fragments, killing all life within 200 metres.

claims.quote: Melinite bombs will turn to dust farmhouses, villages, and hamlets, destroying everything that might be used as cover, obstacle, or refuge.
claims.description: High-explosive bombs will obliterate all structures on the battlefield.
